verdict.summary: Zscaler's fiscal Q3 quarter combined 25% revenue and ARR growth with record adjusted profitability, but the organic rate was lower. Revenue was $850.5M, ARR $3.525B and net-new ARR $166M; excluding Red Canary, ARR grew 21% and net-new ARR 14%. GAAP operating loss was $29.6M against $195.8M non-GAAP income, while free cash flow reached $136M. FY2026 revenue guidance rose to $3.3295B-$3.3325B, but expected FCF margin fell to 22.8%-23.3% as capex increased. The dated valuation is 8.6x ARR with a 2.5% guided FCF yield. September 3 earnings impose an absolute veto: $188.18 activation and $181.69 stop are inactive pending review. If retained, $198.50 and $203.1999 are prior swing highs. Organic ARR and cash margin must survive the investment cycle.

business.overview:
Zscaler sells cloud-delivered Zero Trust subscriptions that connect users, devices and workloads to applications without exposing the underlying network. Revenue expands through customer additions, seats, data protection, workload security and higher platform bundles. ARR and net-new ARR are the most direct demand measures.

The AI transmission channel is access control for users, agents, data and applications. AI agents create non-human identities and more east-west communication that must be inspected and governed. Zscaler can monetize this through Zero Trust Exchange, data security, Red Canary and access-graph capabilities rather than selling generic AI infrastructure.

The model breaks if customers standardize on bundled Microsoft or network-vendor security, if acquired products fail to cross-sell, or if capex rises faster than consumption. Red Canary already lifts headline ARR above the organic rate. Zscaler must preserve renewal, net-new ARR and cash margin while moving into broader security operations; otherwise platform expansion produces accounting complexity without proportional per-share value.
business.moat: Zscaler's cloud proxy architecture, global enforcement network and accumulated policy integrations create switching costs and avoid backhauling traffic through customer networks. The moat is strongest in large distributed estates, but bundled identity, endpoint and SASE offerings can compress standalone pricing.

earnings.beatNote: Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was $850.5M (+25%), ARR $3.525B (+25%) and net-new ARR $166M. Excluding Red Canary, ARR grew 21% and net-new ARR 14%. GAAP operating loss was $29.6M versus $195.8M non-GAAP income; FCF was $136M. Management expects $875M-$878M of fiscal Q4 revenue and $3.3295B-$3.3325B for FY2026. Caveat: FY2026 FCF-margin guidance fell to 22.8%-23.3%, and September 3 results will replace this outlook.
